alt: Detailed summary of an OCR/HHS civil rights complaint against L.A. Care regarding medical records access.
summary: This document provides the exhaustive technical and narrative details of a civil rights complaint filed with the HHS Office for Civil Rights (OCR). It outlines specific violations related to the Right to Access medical records under HIPAA and the Knox-Keene Act, detailing L.A. Care's failure to provide timely and complete access to forensic evidence. The summary serves as a central evidentiary exhibit linking administrative negligence to broader civil rights and privacy protections.

* How and why do you believe the HIPAA Rules were violated? Please be as specific as possible.

On Monday, May 25, 2026, | contacted Inland Psychiatric Medical Group to schedule a telehealth intake
for complex medication management. | explicitly provided the intake coordinator with my current, active
cell phone number. The coordinator looked up my profile using my health plan Member ID, which
evidently pulled up an outdated, historical profile containing an old contact number belonging to my
father.

The coordinator never verified that an incorrect phone number was on file. The clinic transmitted my
protected health information (PHI) - specifically my confidential psychiatric intake forms and telehealth
appointment access links - via SMS text message to my father’s phone number without my
authorization or consent, starting on Monday, May 25 at 12:52 PM and again on Tuesday, May 26 at
9:08 AM.

My privacy was compromised, but to ensure | could receive care, | completed the intake paperwork
after it was forwarded to me. On Tuesday, May 26, 2026, at 11:49 AM - exactly 41 minutes prior to my
12:30 PM appointment - | verbally contacted the clinic’s front desk to explicitly confirm they had
everything and to request the video link, which I had not received on my device. Despite this live
confirmation call, the clinic failed to send the video link to my correct number, resulting in a severe delay
and immediate disruption to the start of my medical care.
